observations:
Torah 223 contains only one explicit bechina statement connecting two concepts: (1) the tzaddik who decrees (צַדִּיק שֶׁיָּכוֹל לִגְזֹר) and (2) the Priestly Blessing formula 'כֹּה תְבָרְכוּ... אָמוֹר לָהֶם.' This pair forms Package 1 in torah_223_packages.json (proposed from gap analysis, since the dataset has no entries for reference 223).

The threshold for a new package — 3 or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain — is not met. The Torah text uses bechina language exactly once ('וְזֶה בְּחִינַת'), yielding only a 2-node pair.

The contrasting concept mentioned in the text — the ordinary tzaddik who petitions (בַּקָּשָׁה), whose request may or may not be heard — uses no bechina language and is structurally a foil/contrast, not a bechina-connected node. It cannot be grouped into a package.

There is no evil mirror in this Torah. The Torah discusses a hierarchy within holiness (ordinary tzaddik vs. higher tzaddik), not a good/evil polarity. No evil package is warranted.

Conclusion: The existing single package (Package 1) from gap analysis covers the entire conceptual content of Torah 223. No additional packages are needed or supported by the text.
